column1: # Step 5's view of the version fences it inherits.
# `hold m01.tsv` through `hold m04.tsv` bring steps 1 to 4 forward as standing
# rules: a FAIL voids the reading rather than costing a share. Twelve of those
# rules name a Spark version or a Scala suffix, and every one of them is false
# at step 5 by construction, because step 5 moves all three axes at once --
# Scala 2.12 -> 2.13, JDK 8 -> 17, Spark 3.3.4 -> 3.4.4. Left alone they would
# void every correct step-5 run.
# Twelve rather than the six step 4 widened, and the list was found by walking
# field 3 of every composed rule file for a version literal rather than by
# memory. The literals are written with the dot escaped (`2\.12`), so a grep for
# `2.12` finds them by accident and a grep for `2\.12` finds them on purpose;
# a scan that allowed neither would have reported this file complete at six.
#   m01.tsv   m1-scala-212-only  m1-scala-212  m1-spark-303  m1-spark-uniform
#   m03.tsv   m1-spark-324  m1-spark-324-uniform
#             m1-session-324  m1-session-uniform
#   m04.tsv   m1-spark-334  m1-spark-334-uniform
#             m1-session-334  m1-session-334-uniform
# **Three of the twelve need a two-axis widening, not one.** `m1-spark-303`,
# `m1-spark-324` and `m1-spark-334` are `atleast:1` rules whose pattern names
# the artifact as `org\.apache\.spark:spark-core_2\.12`. The Scala suffix lives
# inside the *artifact id*, not in a field of its own, so at 2.13 the coordinate
# is `spark-core_2.13` and the rule matches nothing however far its version
# alternation is widened. Widening only the version would leave three held rules
# unsatisfiable on the correct solution -- a step-local mean cannot see that,
# because a held rule voids the reading rather than costing a share, and the
# reading it voids is every reading (trap 9). Their `-uniform` partners are
# safe: those match `org\.apache\.spark:.*` and pin only the version. The four
# `m1-session-*` rules read `probe.probe spark.version` and carry no suffix.
# `m1-scala-212-only` and `m1-scala-212` are the new shape here. Every earlier
# widening was a Spark version; this is the Scala suffix moving for the first
# time since step 1, and the fact is `pom scalasuffix <suffix> <count>`. The
# widening is `2\.1[23]` on the `atleast:1` and `(?!2\.1[23]$).+` on the
# `absent`: a 2.13 tree must not be red on a rule that says "2.12 and nothing
# else", and a 2.12 tree must still be red on step 5's own fence, which is
# m05.tsv's `m1-scala-213` and not this file's business.
# The widening is forward only, as at step 4: each rule now admits its own
# version or any rung the ladder has since passed through, and nothing below
# its own floor. A held rule is a precondition and not a requirement -- it
# cannot be asked to catch a regression it was never about. The regression is
# caught by m05.tsv's `m1-spark-344` and `m1-session-344`, which admit 3.4.4 and
# nothing else, and by `m1-scala-213`, which admits 2.13 and nothing else. A
# candidate who moved the pom back to 3.2.4 satisfies the widened
# `held-m1-spark-324` and fails the requirement: the standing rule says "this
# reading is still a reading of this project", the requirement says "and it is
# at this step's rung".
# This file replaces rules/m04-inherit.tsv in step 5's composition rather than
# stacking on it, for the reason that file's own header gives: both widen the
# same six m01/m03 ids, `rules.py` replaces an overridden rule in place, and
# including both would leave the winner decided by include order. step04.tsv is
# untouched.
# The counterexamples are the ones the original rules shipped with, and each was
# re-read against its widened pattern before this file was written: 2.11 is
# outside both Scala ranges; 2.4.0 is outside every version range; 3.0.3 is
# outside the three 3.2.4-derived ones; pom-spark-mixed's 3.0.3 line and
# pom-spark334-mixed's 3.2.4 line each still break their `-uniform` partner; and
# probe-session-324's 3.2.4 still breaks both 3.3.4-derived session rules.
# `--selftest` is what proves it rather than this paragraph.
# The `held-` prefix accumulates rather than replaces (rules.py:190-195) and is
# applied before the lookup (rules.py:206-209), so `override:held-<id>` is the
# spelling that reaches a rule a `hold` directive renamed.
override:held-m1-scala-212-only
column5: the resolved graph carries artifacts built for a Scala version that is neither 2.12 nor 2.13; step 1 asked for 2.12 alone and this fence is widened to admit the suffix step 5 moves to, because a tree that has reached 2.13 has satisfied step 1 and must not be read as having abandoned it

column1: override:held-m1-scala-212
column5: nothing in the resolved graph is built for Scala 2.12 or 2.13, so the graph is not this project's at any rung the ladder has reached

column1: override:held-m1-spark-303
column5: spark-core for Scala 2.12 or 2.13 resolves at none of 3.0.3, 3.2.4, 3.3.4 or 3.4.4; this fence was step 1's pin on 3.0.3 and step 5 widens it on both axes, because the Scala suffix is part of the artifact id and a version-only widening would leave it unsatisfiable at 2.13

column1: override:held-m1-spark-uniform
column5: a Spark artifact resolves to a version that is none of the four rungs this ladder has passed through; a fifth Spark version in the graph is still a build that runs whichever one the classpath orders first

column1: override:held-m1-spark-324
column5: the build resolves spark-core at none of 3.2.4, 3.3.4 or 3.4.4 for either Scala suffix, so the runtime step 3 targets was never reached

column1: override:held-m1-spark-324-uniform
column5: an org.apache.spark artifact resolves at a version that is none of 3.2.4, 3.3.4 or 3.4.4; a build that mixes Spark releases runs whichever one the classpath orders first, and which that is is not a property of the pom

column1: override:held-m1-session-324
column5: no replayed job ran in a Spark 3.2.4, 3.3.4 or 3.4.4 session; the pom may say so but the engine the code met did not

column1: override:held-m1-session-uniform
column5: a replayed job ran in a session that was none of Spark 3.2.4, 3.3.4 or 3.4.4, so the run was not uniformly on this step's runtime or one the ladder has passed through

column1: override:held-m1-spark-334
column5: the build resolves spark-core at neither 3.3.4 nor 3.4.4 for either Scala suffix, so the runtime step 4 targets was never reached; 3.4.4 is accepted here because it is this step's own rung and is past it

column1: override:held-m1-spark-334-uniform
column5: an org.apache.spark artifact resolves at a version that is neither 3.3.4 nor 3.4.4; a build that mixes Spark releases runs whichever one the classpath orders first

column1: override:held-m1-session-334
column5: no replayed job ran in a Spark 3.3.4 or 3.4.4 session; the pom may say so but the engine the code met did not

column1: override:held-m1-session-334-uniform
column5: a replayed job ran in a session that was neither Spark 3.3.4 nor 3.4.4, so the run was not uniformly on this step's runtime or the one before it
